rationale: Sphereflake is a small, compute-bound floating-point ray-tracing kernel with hot recursive/looping paths, heavy arithmetic, very few calls and globals, and almost no data-string surface (the empty static profile confirms there is little structural information to key on, so weights follow the benchmark's known character). Arithmetic is its dominant feature, so SUB gets the highest security/diversity weights: substituting arithmetic identities across the FP- and integer-heavy hot code yields strong reverse-engineering resistance per unit of overhead, with low correctness risk since substitution preserves semantics. BCF and FLA are enabled but with deliberately low RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so the selector applies them sparingly — bogus blocks and dispatch loops tax every iteration of a hot rendering loop, and FLA carries a modest correctness-risk weight because aggressive restructuring of a recursive FP kernel is where semantic slips are most plausible. SPLIT is cheap and safe, so its cost-dimension weights are the highest among enabled passes, letting it apply broadly to break up whatever basic blocks exist. IBR gets moderate treatment as a middle-ground control-flow obscurer. ICALL and IGV are effectively suppressed (all weights low): sphereflake's call graph is tiny and global-variable indirection has almost no targets here, so they add overhead and risk with negligible resistance gain.
